Stir Fry Eighteen is a game about cooking stir fry while deceiving your opponents and trying to score the most points at the table. Players draw additional cards each turn by discarding either pairs of matching ingredients or "protein cards” face down. Each player draws a card each turn and then may discard face down ingredients to draw more cards. Chefs at the table can call for a Taste Test and flip these cards over! Catching another chef using false ingredients is super tasty and grants you an extra card but beware, wrongly accusing a chef will cost you all of the cards in your hand! Additionally, Stir Fry Eighteen can be a mouthful so we've taken to calling it " #SF18 " as you may see in the rules. Card Frequencies and Values There are 18 cards: 1 - Shrimp (6 points, 9 points with Ginger, 11 points with Soy Sauce and Ginger, when discarded gives 4 cards) 1 - Pork (5 points, 8 points with Mushrooms, when discarded gives 3 cards) 1 - Chicken (3 points, 5 points with Green Onion, 7 points with Ginger and Green Onion, when discarded gives 2 cards) 2 - Ginger (2 points, 4 points with Pork) 2 - Green Onion (3 points, 5 points with Shrimp) 3 - Soy Sauce (1 point, 2 points with Green Onion, 3 points with Ginger) 3 - Mushrooms (2 points, 3 points with Chicken) 5 - Noodles (1 point) How to Play: Shuffle the #SF18 deck and deal three cards to each chef. The chef who most recently ate stir fry goes first! At the beginning of your turn draw a card from the deck. There is no maximum hand size during your turn or another chef’s turn. You MUST discard down to three cards at the end of your turn. The following includes the actions players may take, instructions on cooking, how to end your turn, and all about bluffing your fellow chefs or calling their taste tests! Chef’s Actions Discarding to draw new cards : Discarding is done face down and bluffing is encouraged. Discard a pair of matching ingredients to draw 3 cards. (May only be done once per turn) You do not have to name the pairs you discard out loud. Discard a “protein” (chicken, pork, or shrimp) card to draw the value listed on the card. (May only be done once per turn) Note that you can only do one of EACH discard type per turn, but may do BOTH every turn if you choose to. Cook a Stir Fry You may cook 3-5 different ingredients once per turn. (no less than 3, no more than 5). You must have noodles as one ingredient in your stir fry. No two like ingredients may be cooked in a single stir fry. If the deck runs out it is NOT reshuffled until you have cooked. Count your ingredient and bonus scores and record your total. (Take only the single highest value for any bonus.) End of Turn Gather all played and/or discarded cards and shuffle them into the deck. If you cooked this turn draw a card. You may pass if you cannot or do not want to cook. If you have more than three cards, discard down to three and shuffle the deck again. Bluffing and Taste Tests Bluffing is encouraged but your fellow chefs may call a taste test! Taste test is when a chef claims you’ve lied about your discard. community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Draw cards and hope that they can be combined to a high-scoring recipe. There is a bluffing mechanism for drawing new cards but bluffing is very risky if someone calls it, reducing the game the luck of the draw.

[Rating: 3/10] Often times not enough attractive options during one's turn.  Getting a bluff wrong is too punishing.  Game can feel a bit like just pushing and counting cards if bluffs are rare.

[Rating: 3/10] Push your luck with 18 cards, players are trying to gather ingredient combinations that give them the most points. Includes bluffing and randomness.  I felt that the cards in my hand often gave me an obvious choice of what to do on my turn so in the end it felt like the game was playing itself. The visuals of the cards aren't very intuitive, you always have to read the text. Chopstick font is of bad taste.

[Rating: 3/10] I've only played this game once and it took 50 minutes with 5 players. It dragged on too long for what it is and the risk-reward-ratio in calling somebody on a bluff just didn't feel right to me.  I have little to no information if somebody is actually bluffing, it's more of a random guess with some people reading, but if I'm wrong I lose all my cards and have pretty much a dead turn when it's my turn, if I'm right a draw 1 additional card.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA. Super boring game. Likely won't draw what you need, and people are likely to call you out when you bluff to try to get more than one card on a turn, so you're just stuck blind drawing a card and hoping you get something useful most of the game.   Might be a bit better in person but I just don't see why I would ever want to play this over Sushi Go! or Cockroach Poker.

[Rating: 3/10] A card based game where players are pushing their playing/bluffing their cards to draw more cards in order to make dishes/hands to score points.

[Rating: 4/10] Cute, simply bluffing card game. I'm so bad at bluffing so it's rough for me, but it's a good game overall.
